subject: Merlin Health pilot — recommended model shortlist, perf links & kickoff
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Alyssa Chen <alyssa.chen@merlinhealth.com>, Tom Burke <tom.burke@merlinhealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 29 Jun 2027 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Merlin pilot — model options & perf targets

Thanks again for the time today — quick recap and a proposed small model slate to start the pilot. Nice discovery: your primary goals are (1) reduce time-to-answer in care ops workflows, (2) maintain <2% critical hallucination rate on KB-grounded Q&A, and (3) average response latency <= 200ms for short queries.

Recommended model shortlist (Redwood-verified profiles attached and linked):
- rwin/compact-12B-ql: throughput-focused; typical batch=8; test profile (seq=64): ~95 TPS, p50=22ms, p95=58ms, p99=130ms. Good for heavy throughput when you prioritize cost.
- rwin/mesa-16B-fp16: quality-first; seq=256 test profile: 18 TPS, p50=45ms, p95=120ms, p99=240ms. Stronger on KB grounding and few-shot retrieval.
- rwin/mixlite-8B-q4: balanced; seq=128: ~210 TPS, p50=16ms, p95=48ms, p99=95ms. Best trade for interactive workflows.

Notes on the numbers: these are Redwood-verified on our dedicated inference runtime using representative request shapes from your call (short Q&A bursts + occasional long contexts). Full perf traces and raw TPS traces are in the attached merlin_eval_summary_v1.csv and at the bench link below.

Quality / regression concerns we raised on the call:
- Hallucination measurement: we'll baseline using your KB-grounded evaluation set (please confirm the KB subset you want included). We recommend gating canary releases by critical hallucination rate <= 2% on that set.
- Prompt sensitivity: we observed certain prompt patterns amplify hallucination on mesa-16B during synthetic tests; we'll include a 10-prompt guardrail prompt set for regression checks (attached merlin_prompt_set_v1.txt).

Proposed immediate next steps (30-day pilot kickoff plan):
1) You confirm the KB subset and share access to a small sample (10–50 docs).
2) We run a 3-model smoke benchmark (compact-12B, mixlite-8B, mesa-16B) on your shapes and share TPS/latency + quality scores (2 business days).
3) Agree on success metrics and canary rollout cadence.
4) Kickoff call: 30 minutes where we review the bench results and agree on the pilot SLA.

Suggested kickoff windows: Thu 7/1 10:00–11:00 PT or Fri 7/2 09:00–09:30 PT. If those don't work, propose times and we'll adjust.

Links/attachments referenced: Redwood bench pack (https://redwood.app/bench/merlin/2027-06), merlin_eval_summary_v1.csv, merlin_prompt_set_v1.txt, and redwood_verified_profiles.pdf.

Thanks — happy to coordinate the NDA/PO steps if you want to move fast.

— Jonas

Jonas — thanks for the clear summary. This reads well and the perf targets are in the right ballpark. A couple quick asks before the smoke run: 

1) Quality monitoring: can Redwood produce continuous regression alerts for the hallucination metric during the pilot (e.g., nightly runs against the validation prompt set)? We need an automatic alert to the Merlin team if critical hallucination >2.5% and an option to auto-roll back to a safer model profile.

2) Data residency: the initial pilot data have PHI-like attributes; can you confirm that the private pilot will not leave our VPC (we discussed Dedicated vs Private briefly)? If not, we'll need a short addendum.

3) Timeline: Thu 7/1 10am PT works for Tom and me. Please send a calendar invite; we'll share the KB subset via a secure Drive link prior to the meeting.

Also, Ben — can you loop in the CS person who will own the onboarding checklist?

Thanks,
Alyssa Chen
